title: Predicting and improving complex beer flavor through machine learning
finding: Gradient boosting models trained on chemical and sensory data from 250 beers plus 180,000 consumer reviews predict flavor and appreciation and reveal specific compounds that drive taste.

title: From Data to Draught: Modelling and Predicting Mixed-Culture Beer Fermentation Dynamics Using Autoregressive Recurrent Neural Networks
finding: Autoregressive recurrent neural networks capture the time-dependent dynamics of mixed-culture beer fermentation and forecast its trajectory better than static models.

title: Enhancing beer authentication, quality, and control assessment using non-invasive spectroscopy through bottle and machine learning modeling
finding: Near-infrared spectroscopy read through the bottle plus machine learning classifies beer fermentation type and authenticity without opening the container.

title: Predictive modeling using artificial intelligence for sensory panel assessments of customized beer production
finding: AI models trained on production parameters predict trained sensory panel scores for customized beers, cutting reliance on full panel sessions.

title: Predicting acetic acid content in the final beer using neural networks and support vector machine
venue: Journal of the Institute of Brewing
finding: Neural networks and support vector machines predict end-of-fermentation acetic acid levels in commercial-scale beer from early process variables.

title: Learning algorithms for identification of whisky using portable Raman spectroscopy
authors: Kwang Jun Lee, Alexander C. Trowbridge, et al.
venue: arXiv (later Current Research in Food Science)
finding: Machine learning on portable Raman spectra identifies whisky brand at over 99 percent accuracy and quantifies ethanol and methanol, even through unopened bottles.

title: Quick insights into whisky: investigating rapid and efficient methods for sensory evaluation and chemical analysis
finding: A linear classifier (OWSum) and a CNN on GC-MS molecular data classify whisky odor attributes and origin, matching or beating human experts and flagging marker compounds like menthol and methyl decanoate.

title: Recent advances in whiskey analysis for authentication, discrimination, and quality control
venue: Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety
finding: A review of analytical and chemometric methods, including machine learning on spectroscopy and chromatography data, for authenticating and grading whiskey.

title: Machine learning-based predictive modelling for the enhancement of wine quality
finding: Ensemble models on physicochemical measurements predict wine quality scores and rank the features that most influence quality.

title: Wine feature importance and quality prediction: A comparative study of machine learning algorithms with unbalanced data
finding: Compares classifiers on imbalanced wine quality data and identifies alcohol, sulphates and volatile acidity as leading quality predictors.

title: Wine Quality Prediction with Ensemble Trees: A Unified, Leak-Free Comparative Study
finding: A leakage-controlled benchmark shows gradient-boosted and random forest ensembles give the most reliable wine quality predictions when evaluation is done cleanly.

title: End-to-end deep learning for directly estimating grape yield from ground-based imagery
venue: Computers and Electronics in Agriculture (arXiv preprint)
finding: Deep models trained on 23,581 yield points and over 100,000 vehicle-mounted images estimate vineyard grape yield directly, comparing detection, CNN regression and transformer architectures.

title: Grape detection, segmentation and tracking using deep neural networks and three-dimensional association
venue: arXiv (later Computers and Electronics in Agriculture)
finding: CNNs detect, segment and track grape clusters in the field with F1 up to 0.91, enabling automated berry counting for yield estimation.

title: Digital Assessment and Classification of Wine Faults Using a Low-Cost Electronic Nose, Near-Infrared Spectroscopy and Machine Learning Modelling
finding: A low-cost electronic nose and NIR spectra with machine learning detect and classify wine faults at 90 to 97 percent accuracy for red and white wines.

title: Machine Learning in Fine Wine Price Prediction
finding: Gaussian process regression and multi-task learning on Liv-Ex 100 price histories forecast fine wine prices more accurately than ARMA and GARCH baselines.

title: From Words to Ratings: Machine Learning and NLP for Wine Reviews
finding: Transformer embeddings of expert tasting notes predict wine ratings and show that language markers such as complexity and harmony track higher expert scores.

title: Learning to Taste: A Multimodal Wine Dataset (WineSensed)
finding: Introduces WineSensed, 897k label images and 824k reviews plus human flavor-distance rankings, to learn joint representations of wine vision, language and flavor.

title: Multiclass classification of diseased grape leaf identification using deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) classifier
finding: A deep CNN classifies grapevine leaf images into healthy and diseased classes such as black rot, esca and leaf blight for early vineyard disease detection.
